newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina says estimates '96 budget deficit $5 bln.
newsitem.headline: Argentina says estimates '96 budget deficit $5 bln.

text.p: Argentina should end 1996 with a budget deficit of $5 billion, Finance Secretary Pablo Guidotti said Thursday.
Argentina has a deficit target agreed with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) of $2.5 billion.
"Our projections are that we are going to finish the year with a deficit of about $5 billion," Guidotti told reporters.
He added that $4 billion of the deficit would be financed by debt but that, with regards to the remaining $1 billion, "we are studying alternatives."

He said that the IMF was not demanding as a condition for reaching a new agreement with Argentina that Congress approve in October a package of fiscal measures announced in August by Economy Minister Roque Fernandez. But he added that the government does hope the package will be approved in October, and that it will pass the Lower House by mid-September.
Guidotti said that "the financing necessities of 1996 are going to be covered without problems. We are seeing that the attitude of capital markets towards Argentina is positive.
"They are offering financing at very favorable terms and we do not foresee any sort of problems."
He added that the Economy Ministry is "working intensely so that 1997 budget spending stays at the same levels it was in 1996", around $41.5 billion.
"We will send a conservative budget to Congress on September 13," Guidotti said.
Guidotti said that the Economy Ministry plans to "profoundly" revise and simplify the taxation system.

He foresaw "fewer taxes with a more coherent structure...more easily understandable to the tax payer and...the opportunity to reduce some taxes," he said. Guidotti added that the system's complexity encouraged evasion.

"What we are not going to do is try and reduce taxes hoping that revenues will increase," he said, "We want a solid and predictable fiscal situation that is going to help lower Argentina's risk." He added, "Our intention is to continue reducing taxes on labor and value-added tax."
